titulo: Original GTA Artist Says He's 'Flattered' to See His Influence Continue in GTA 6 Cover Art
texto: Stephen Bliss, the former Rockstar Games artist who helped establish Grand Theft Auto's iconic visual style, has said he's flattered to see elements of his original designs continue to appear in the cover art for GTA 6.

titulo: Artist With Music In GTA 6 Had No Idea About Any Of That

Richard, 86, didn't know about any of that, however, or that GTA 6 is a game and not a TV show. Speaking to The Times ( via Dexerto ), Richard said of the partnership with Rockstar for GTA 6: "I was told this happened!" He said his nephew's sons told him about it. titulo: GTA 6’s Cops Will Send Dogs To Get You
texto: The police in GTA 6 are smarter and more capable than they were in GTA 5, and that includes the newly confirmed detail that cops can dispatch dogs to hunt you down. Edge Magazine recently posted a preview of the game with Rockstar's Rob Nelson playing. In one sequence, Jason and Lucia are attempting to evade police when they crash their motorcycle and try to escape on foot. However, nearby cops send out a K9 unit to assist. One of the dogs, a German Shepherd, quickly grabs Jason and pins him to the ground. According to Edge, developers standing by during the preview urged Nelson not to shoot the dog. This implies that it's possible to shoot police dogs, and that wouldn't be surprising, as GTA 5 lets you shoot and kill dogs as well. titulo: GTA 6 Makes A Familiar Open-World Gaming Feature Work In Its Own Way
texto: One feature Grand Theft Auto 6 borrows from modern-day open-world games is the ability to call a ride whenever you need it, but in true Rockstar fashion, it comes with a bit of real-life friction. It's not quite as simple as hitting a button to " even the odds " when you need to make a fast getaway. As GamesRadar's GTA 6 cover story details, you'll have the option to summon your car via a smartphone app. It won't magically appear, as the Scooter Bros. app will see a company employee drop your vehicle off at your location--for a small fee, of course. Just like the car drop-off services you'll find in real life, these couriers have a compact scooter stashed in the trunk of your car, and they'll ride off into the sunset once they've done their job.
